chapter_title: Checking and Calibrating AI Agent Output
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of three agents may be used as a first pass, may be used only to draft evidence, or should not be used, and name the measure on the calibration dashboard that decided it, with at least 5 of 6 decisions correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** calibration-dashboard-reader
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of three agents may be used as a first pass, may be used only to draft evidence, or should not be used, and name the measure on the calibration dashboard that decided it, with at least 5 of 6 decisions correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Calibration Against Humans, Agreement Rate, Mean Absolute Difference, Score Correlation, Cohen's Kappa, Run-to-Run Variance, Prompt Refinement (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each agent the learner makes two decisions: how the agent may be used, and which measure decided it. A decision is correct when it matches the Content table. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 decisions correct on the first attempt. Reading the standard is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The best single measure decides everything. (2) A high correlation is enough. (3) An agent that fails the standard is useless. **Instructional Rationale:** Deciding how an agent may be used from a set of measures is an Evaluate-level action. Three agents that each fail, or pass, for a different reason teach the learner to find the measure that matters. **Content:** The standard, shown at all times (illustrative, labeled "illustrative standard"): first pass requires all of these: agreement rate at a threshold of 1 >= 80 percent, absolute bias <= 0.5, mean absolute difference <= 1.0, and the adoption decision matches the humans. An agent that fails any one of them may be used only to draft evidence for a person to check. An agent whose adoption decision differs from the humans and whose absolute bias is > 0.5 should not be used until the prompt is refined. The dashboard covers one resource, so it shows the adoption decision and not kappa or the run-to-run range, which need many resources or many runs. The dashboard, one row per agent (the numbers come from the chapter's running example): | Agent | Agreement at threshold 1 | Mean absolute difference | Bias | Correlation | Adoption decision (humans: Revise) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A1 | 100 percent | 1.0 | +1.0 | 1.00 | Adopt | | A2 | 100 percent | 0.3 | -0.1 | 0.96 | Revise | | A3 | 40 percent | 1.4 | 0.0 | 0.46 | Revise | The decisions: | Agent | Correct use | Deciding measure | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | A1 | Should not be used until the prompt is refined | Bias | The bias is +1.0, which exceeds 0.5, and the adoption decision differs from the humans. | | A2 | May be used as a first pass | None fails | Every measure is within the standard. | | A3 | May be used only to draft evidence | Agreement rate | Its agreement rate of 40 percent is < 80 percent, and its decision matches the humans. | The three uses, offered as choices: May be used as a first pass; May be used only to draft evidence; Should not be used until the prompt is refined. The deciding measures, offered as choices: Agreement rate; Mean absolute difference; Bias; Correlation; Adoption decision; None fails. **Provenance:** The numbers come from the chapter's running example and are labeled "illustrative examples". The standard is an illustrative choice for the book, and the sim labels it "illustrative standard". **Rules:** Each agent has exactly one correct use and one correct deciding measure. The deciding measure is the first failing measure in this order: agreement rate, mean absolute difference, bias, adoption decision. Correlation never decides. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the dashboard and the standard. 2. For the highlighted agent the learner chooses a use and a deciding measure. 3. The sim shows whether each choice was correct and the Why text. 4. After the third agent the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 3 agents in a shuffled order, two decisions each, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The correct use is [use], decided by [measure]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 decisions correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can read a calibration dashboard." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed agent. **Starting State:** The dashboard, the standard, and the first agent highlighted. **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's calibration steps, the illustrative standard, and the refinement from Agent A1 to Agent A2 give the numbers and the standard used in this sim.
